title: The effect of ChatGPT on students’ learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking: insights from a meta-analysis
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether ChatGPT improves student learning outcomes and under what conditions its effects are strongest. The authors note that prior studies and reviews produced mixed conclusions, with some reporting benefits and others finding null or negative effects. To resolve these inconsistencies, they conducted a meta-analysis of 51 experimental or quasi-experimental studies published between November 2022 and February 2025.

The review focuses on ChatGPT used as an educational support tool in learning settings, including higher education, secondary education, and a small amount of primary education. The included studies span STEM and related courses, language learning and academic writing, and skills/competencies development, with ChatGPT deployed in personalized learning, problem-based learning, project-based learning, contextual learning, reflective learning, and mixed formats. The control conditions were required to exclude ChatGPT and rely on traditional or comparable non-ChatGPT learning methods.

The meta-analysis finds that ChatGPT has a large positive overall effect on learning performance and moderate positive effects on learning perception and higher-order thinking. Moderator analyses suggest that learning performance benefits are strongest in skills/competencies courses, problem-based learning, and 4–8 week interventions; learning perception benefits increase with longer duration, especially beyond 8 weeks; and higher-order thinking gains are strongest in STEM courses and when ChatGPT serves as an intelligent tutor. The authors conclude that ChatGPT can support learning, but its effectiveness depends on course type, instructional model, duration, and how it is used pedagogically.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis of 51 experimental/quasi-experimental studies with explicit inclusion criteria, effect-size computation, heterogeneity tests, publication-bias checks, and sensitivity analyses. That makes it high-credibility evidence for the general effect of ChatGPT in education, though the included studies vary widely in context and quality.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effects on learning performance (g=0.867), learning perception (g=0.456), and higher-order thinking (g=0.457) are all at least moderate, with learning performance large. Although this paper is not middle-school mathematics-specific, the magnitude and consistency of effects indicate substantial positive impact on educational outcomes overall.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as a generative AI tutor/assistant across experimental studies, supporting students through tutoring, assessment and feedback, personalized recommendations, and conversational problem solving in varied courses.

finding.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 44 independent studies found that ChatGPT improved learning performance with a large overall effect (Hedges's g=0.867, 95% CI [0.683, 1.052]). The included studies used post-test means/SDs or equivalent statistics from experimental vs control groups, with outcomes spanning STEM, language, and skills courses; the paper reports high heterogeneity (I²=89.243%).
finding.measure: Learning performance measured primarily by tests and exams

finding.finding_summary: Across 19 independent studies, ChatGPT had a moderate positive effect on learning perception (g=0.456, 95% CI [0.287, 0.625]). Outcomes were assessed with scales/questionnaires capturing perceptions, with moderate heterogeneity (I²=72.580%); longer interventions (>8 weeks) showed larger effects.
finding.measure: Learning perception measured by scales and questionnaires

finding.finding_summary: For higher-order thinking, 9 independent studies showed a moderate positive effect of ChatGPT (g=0.457, 95% CI [0.255, 0.650]). The outcome was measured via scales/questionnaires targeting higher-order thinking, with moderate heterogeneity (I²=55.813%); effects were strongest when ChatGPT acted as an intelligent tutor.
finding.measure: Higher-order thinking measured by scales and questionnaires
